reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's the last Friday of July. Somewhere the version of me that drank is already three drinks in, telling himself he's earned it, that the weekend is what the week was for. I remember that math. I remember how the week became a countdown and the weekend became a blur and Monday became a coffin you climbed out of to start counting again.

What nobody told me back then is that a sober Friday is a small, quiet miracle. Not because it's exciting — most of them aren't. It's a workout, dinner you actually taste, a friend's text you actually answer, the sun going down over a summer you're actually inside of. The excitement, when it comes, is real. The peace, when it comes, is real. Neither of them has to be manufactured.

Durant's line about habit is doing more work than it looks like it's doing. The life I have now wasn't built by one dramatic decision on November 12, 2014. It was built by a thousand ordinary Fridays where I did the next right small thing instead of the old loud thing. Presence is a habit. Showing up is a habit. Being someone your friends can count on is a habit. You don't feel yourself becoming that person. You just wake up one summer and realize you already are.
reflection.meditation: What small, ordinary thing can I show up for today — not because it's exciting, but because it's mine?

affirmations: I am building my life one ordinary day at a time, and today counts.
Today I choose presence over escape, even when the day is quiet.
I am becoming someone my friends, and I, can count on.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Friday I'll remember. I'm grateful for the summer light, for a body that works, for people who know my real name and my real story. I'm grateful for the boredom I used to run from — turns out it was just peace I hadn't learned to sit with yet.
gratitude.closing: One more day, clear-eyed. That's the whole thing.
